influences.name: Outkast
influences.context: "You don't have to play really intense music or do anything different [in a space like that] – I played Outkast."

influences.name: Mahmoud Guinia
influences.context: "For the following release to be a collaboration with the recently deceased Mahmoud Guinia, followed again by the compositional focus of 'Eleania'"

influences.name: Ade Fakile
influences.context: When it comes to the latter, he credits a lot of his approach to Ade Fakile, the founder of Plastic People

influences.name: Pharoah Sanders
influences.context: Here is the Pharoah Sanders record I was listening to a week earlier at home. Then he's playing it and everyone is jumping up and down, spinning around, going crazy. It was really wild.

influences.name: Talk Talk
influences.context: That was Talk Talk, a big pop band. It's their last record [Spirit of Eden]. It means a lot to a lot of people... It was a bit of a turning point just in a sort of introspective music.

influences.name: Phil Brown
influences.context: The guy who recorded it is Phil Brown, and he wrote a book about a lot of the work he did in recording... I heard that and I was like, 'OK, that's how I'm going to record drums now.' I did a record... and I recorded the drums in the same way and I was trying to copy that, the way that record sounded.

influences.name: Debussy
influences.context: At the time a lot of French impressionist, so Debussy, Messiaen... I saw a lot of harmonic similarity in the way a sort of Bill Evans voicing, Keith Jarrett sort of voicing would be the way Debussy would treat harmony. That was a bridge

influences.name: Gershwin
influences.context: I saw so much similarity, I actually scored a soft landing into the world of jazz. That's when the record-buying started... and maybe even some Gershwin and Bernstein

influences.name: Bernstein

influences.name: Les Chisnall
influences.context: And had a good piano teacher Les Chisnall and Steve Barry. They were really instrumental in focusing me, quite early on, in really good jazz. I'm indebted to them.

influences.name: Steve Barry
influences.context: And had a good piano teacher Les Chisnall and Steve Barry. They were really instrumental in focusing me, quite early on, in really good jazz. I'm indebted to them.

influences.name: Theo Parrish
influences.context: Who made me start taking it seriously was people like Ade [Fakile] from Plastic People, Theo [Parrish] at Plastic... The people who gave me the confidence to really... were people like Ade, Theo, and the other nights going on at Plastic

influences.name: Azymuth
influences.context: That record, yeah. I mean, there's so many records that I heard in that space that informed the way I would try and make music... Azymuth's first album... informed the way I would try and make music.

influences.name: Sean McAuliffe
influences.context: It was Sean McAuliffe, who's a part of the Nonsense Crew from Plastic People, he played it on a radio show once. And he played 'Jail Cell,' which I just couldn't believe it

influences.name: Mark and Mike Grusane
influences.context: That sort of advice you get from a guy at a shop, like Peabody's Records, Mark and Mike Grusane will always beat a Juno recommendation... It's going to be way more wild, you're going to find way more wild music in that process.

influences.name: DJ Love On The Run
influences.context: Through this record, I met a lot of people through gaining these records, like DJ Love On The Run from New York, DJ McBoing Boing from New York... They've taught me so much about this music and so I am highly indebted to them for this sort of knowledge.

influences.name: Jeremy Underground
influences.context: Through this record, I met a lot of people through gaining these records... Jeremy Underground Paris, as well, he's really into this stuff... these guys have taught me a lot about this music.

influences.name: Pearl Girls

influences.name: Red Greg
influences.context: Through this record, I met a lot of people through gaining these records... Red Greg as well, in London, these guys have taught me a lot about this music.

influences.name: Julia
influences.context: The way I'm thinking about it is late, mid- to late '70s soul... my friend Julia showed me this record about five years ago, and it was such a mad turning point for me

influences.name: John Wood
influences.context: My professor, John Wood, he's an amazing guy who was very, very supportive of all my musical endeavors as well

influences.name: James Holden
influences.context: And James Holden was there as well, we were working together on a lot of stuff.
